rationale.conceptual: The work applies a standard DREIDING force field in LAMMPS with a trivial parameter variation and linear fitting of stress-strain data. No new models or complex mathematics are required.
rationale.execution: The pipeline is multi-step: for each epsilon, build an amorphous configuration, perform six-stage equilibration (minimization, NVT, NPT, cooling, etc.), then three uniaxial deformations. Setting up LAMMPS input files, handling ensemble changes, and building the initial amorphous cell (which may require non-trivial packing) makes this a moderately orchestrated execution task.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper presents a straightforward molecular dynamics parameter sweep of van der Waals epsilon and its effect on polymer Young's modulus. Conceptually, it uses standard force fields and simulation protocols; the main difficulty is careful equilibration and tensile testing, but no new theory or algorithms. Execution involves a multi-stage pipeline: building amorphous cell, six-step equilibration, and tri-axial tensile tests for each epsilon, requiring LAMMPS scripting and environment setup.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The simulation system is only 9902 atoms, with a classical force field; CPU-only LAMMPS runs are negligible in memory (under 1 GB) and disk. No large datasets; input force field files are tiny.
